findings.claim: The repair's central new claim — that the seven properties are stated once and referred to everywhere else — is false in its own text: ADR-019 §6 restates item 2 twice in full, and README restates items 3 and 7, one of them inside the sentence asserting "restated nowhere".
findings.evidence: The claim: ADR-019:167-168 "One list, in one place; every other sentence in this file and in README refers to it instead of restating it"; same at :48-49 and INDEX.md:28. Counter-evidence in the same file: ADR-019:254-257 restates item 2's first clause in full with no reference to item 2; :264-269 restates item 2's second clause, also unreferenced — the exact wording R15 found stale at §2:68-73 last round, now living 80 lines below the list instead of 100 lines above it. In README: :107-109 restates item 7 inside the sentence denying restatement; :121 "Same ceiling, not `published >= ledger max`" restates item 3's parenthetical verbatim. The `ponytail:` limit at src/browser/eval_adapter.py:3398-3405 leans on this defence explicitly, so the blacklist's stated backstop is not in place.
findings.repro: sed -n '167,171p;254,276p' specs/decisions/ADR-019-...md; sed -n '104,122p' README.md — compare against §6 items 2, 3 and 7 at :173-186. No eval case can go red on this: `describes_a_deleted_rule` blacklists three retired phrases, and a correct-today restatement is by construction not on that list.
findings.acceptance: Either the two §6 paragraphs (:254-262, :264-276) and README:107-109/:121 defer to the item numbers instead of restating their content ("item 2 is why", as :192-194 and :220 already do), or the single-source sentences at ADR-019:167-168, :48-49 and INDEX.md:28 are narrowed to what is true. Grepping §6 for a sentence that states an item's content without naming its number returns nothing, or the claim no longer says otherwise.

findings.claim: The renumbering from `property N` to `§6 item N` stopped at comments and missed the two strings that reach a reader, so a red `published-band-slack-is-declared` report names §6 items that are off by one.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:676 emits `r21_underpublished_band_green_on_property_2` and :680 emits `r21_underjustified_ceiling_green_on_property_3`. Under §6's list these are item 3 and item 4 (ADR-019:173-186). The comments two lines above each were renumbered by this diff (:673-675), so the comment and the key it guards disagree. The round-3 resolution artifact claims the sweep covered "stale `property 2` / `property 3` numbering in three comments" — the emitted keys were not comments and were not swept.
findings.acceptance: The emitted keys name the same item numbers as §6's list (or no number at all), and no string in `_check_published_band_slack` uses the retired `property N` numbering.

findings.claim: ADR-019 §3 and §6 assert that the 15-deriving band "was published" in this round, and no commit on the branch ever published it; only the greenness half is reproducible.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:101 "that band was published, and the check was GREEN on it" and :236-237 "that exact state was published in this round and the check accepted it". `git log --all -S'12.89 × 1.15'` returns only aeac0f7, the round-4 repair itself quoting it as an example. The bands actually published were 13.22->20, 13.08->20 and 13.32->20; the 12.89/->15 state existed only in an uncommitted working tree. The substantive half IS true and the reviewer verified it: `_band_wrong` returns [] for that state, `round(12.89*1.15,2) == 14.82`, `_band_rule(12.89) == 15 <= 20`.
findings.acceptance: The sentences say what is reproducible — the state was reachable and is green under the current check — rather than that a commit of this PR published it; or a commit sha is cited that did.

findings.claim: §6's list is presented as "exactly what it requires" but omits two properties the code emits, and §2's pointer mis-scopes item 4.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:48-49 "§6 lists exactly what it requires". `_band_wrong` also emits `adr_publishes_no_band_line` (eval_adapter.py:440) and `no_recorded_run_at` (:461), neither in items 1-7. Separately ADR-019:69 says "§6 items 2-4 are what the check requires of it" where "it" is the cited run; item 4 (:179-180) constrains the committed ceiling against the ledger maximum, not the cited run.
